description: Surfaces the morning briefing and the priority signals before you ask — the liquidity watch, the post-merger reconciliation gap, and the seasonality window — correlated across the core, the lending system, finance, and the merged Howard University ledger.

Answers a business-spanning question across every connected source at once, in one query bar over a fused view. Loans versus deposits pulls balances from the core, origination from the lending system, and shares from the finance workbook, and reconciles them into one governed answer.

Shows where sources disagree — above all the Howard University division balances that have not reconciled into the enterprise deposit total — and traces both sides to source on demand, so a gap is visible before it reaches the board rather than after.

Forecasts liquidity if loan demand keeps outpacing deposits, overlays the academic-calendar deposit seasonality as a band rather than a line, and models the effect of a deposit campaign against the internal policy ceiling.

Flags the out-of-pattern: a silent ETL gap that stalled a nightly refresh, a branch deposit figure that breaks its own trend, a concentration drifting past policy. This is the layer catching what used to surface only at month-end.

Drafts the board briefing and the recommended action — a targeted education-community deposit campaign paired with a standby funding line — with owners, timeframes and the evidence attached, then renders it as a board-ready deck.
